paper.title: PoL-BFL: Towards Trustworthy Federated Learning with Zero-Knowledge Proofs and Verifiable Incentives

implementation_choices.clients_per_round: All 50 clients, following Algorithm 1's for-all-client execution.
implementation_choices.update_transport: Deterministic per-tensor symmetric signed four-bit packed transport with lossless stream compression; the paper reports 178.2 MB/round but does not publish its update wire encoding.
implementation_choices.proof_execution: Standard BN254 Groth16 proofs are generated through the locked ICICLE-Snark CUDA backend and independently accepted or rejected by the locked Rapidsnark verifier.
implementation_choices.checkpoint_interval_steps: Chosen as five to match the five-step reference proof relation within the paper's approximately 1.1M-constraint budget.
implementation_choices.hybrid_interval_split: K=2 recent and R=3 random intervals; the paper specifies Q=K+R but does not publish K and R.
implementation_choices.sybil_trajectory_cosine_threshold: 0.995 is a deterministic deployment threshold; sensitivity remains an experimental gate.
implementation_choices.layer_ablation: L1 retains cryptographic training verification; L2 adds statistical screening and Byzantine-robust aggregation; L3 adds committed-trace Sybil/reputation processing and persistent contract enforcement. Disabled economic layers are evaluated without mutating stake or reputation state.
implementation_choices.table5_attack_success: A free-riding attempt succeeds only when the malicious update is included and has positive measured marginal validation accuracy; the aggregate accuracy loss against the same-round honest-only counterfactual is retained separately. No paper outcome value is used by this decision rule.
implementation_choices.table5_participation: Participation rate is the fraction of registered honest clients that execute and submit the round; malicious attack attempts are accounted for separately in ASR.
